title: Which kind of triangle does each set of sides make?
description: Five sets of sidelengths are each built the same way, with the longest side as the base and one arc from each end. The equal sides then tell the kind of each triangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: every set is built with a base and two arcs, and the number of equal sides gives the kind. Watch for children who think a set with one very short side cannot make a triangle.

source: Construct triangles having the following sidelengths: four, four, six; three, four, five; one, five, five; four, six, eight; three point five, three point five, three point five.
video_script.why: The child can build a triangle from three lengths and now builds five of them and sorts them by their equal sides.
video_script.substitution: Each set gives the base, the longest side, and the other two lengths as the two compass openings.
video_script.anchor: Five sets of sidelengths, each to be built as a triangle and named by its kind
video_script.payoff_line: All five triangles can be built, and the kinds are isosceles, scalene, isosceles, scalene and equilateral.

final_answer.spoken: all five can be built, and their kinds are isosceles, scalene, isosceles, scalene and equilateral

hold_back: isosceles, scalene, isosceles, scalene and equilateral
never_show: the full list of five kinds before the answer beat
maths_rules: 1, 5, 5: two equal sides, isosceles, with one very short side
video_script.design: One idea: every set is built with a base and two arcs, and the equal sides give the kind. The five cards stay in the anchor band; the working band lists each kind as it is found.

beats.on_screen: To find: a triangle for each set, and its kind

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, the first set has two equal sides, so it is isosceles.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second set has three different sides, and such a triangle is called scalene.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third set has two equal sides, so it is isosceles with one very short side.

narration: <bookmark mark='fourth'/>Step four, the fourth set has three different sides, so it is scalene.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>The fifth set has three equal sides, so it is equilateral.
